$AKAM signs $11.6B compute deal with Anthropic for accelerated CPU workloads demands over 7 years.

$AMD to $MU should be happy to hear this… 

Akamai ests. ~$5.5B of capex to service the $11.6B commitment. Including +$1.7B of 2026 capex specifically to pre-purchase supply chain components like memory.

So much for Anthropic/OpenAI calling for an AI slowdown?
@aleabitoreddit Never heard $AKAM do you own any? What's the opportunity you see here related to some tickers

Nope for $AKAM. But if you look at what’s needed probably CPUs/Memory #1.

So your $ARM / $INTC / $AMD thematically (AMD probably higher beta to this company in specific). Then your Samsung / $MU / SK Hynix are your obvious memory beneficiaries.

Component procurement is done through $JBL, which potentially benefits their own supply chain if they’re doing networking too.

Okay thing about it for a second:

$AKAM gets a big deal over 7 years. But in order to actually execute on the deal:

They gotta buy a ton of CPUs and memory… So these upstream component supply chains are probably the larger beneficiaries over the ones in the headline.

But can’t give advice in terms of buying something

The cybersecurity threat from agents may be more likely to come from a massed swarm of AIs whose only goal is to penetrate your IT to figure out how much you paid for your company t-shirts as part of a research effort to "find good shirt prices" as it is from bad actor attacks.

This is not a joke. A lot of security specialists are making the wrong assumptions about the ways in which the cybersecurity environment is about to change. All of the swarm attacks from OpenAI seem to be about finding information, usually trivial or mostly irrelevant information
